newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to unveil inflation-linked Treasury bonds.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to unveil inflation-linked Treasury bonds.

text.p: Using an arcane financial instrument for his re-election campaign, President Bill Clinton on Wednesday will outline plans to issue Treasury bonds that are protected against inflation.
Clinton is to announce the plan during a campaign appearance at Robert Morris College in Pittsburgh. The Treasury Department plans to begin offering the new securities in January.
The president is promoting the new bond in terms of helping Americans pay for the cost of education, but officials stressed they might also help families save for retirement or first homes.

They will be offered in denominations as low as $1,000, putting them within the reach of average Americans. The bonds will offer protection against inflation by having an interest rate that is pegged to the rate of inflation, as opposed to regular Treasury bonds, whose fixed interest loses value when the cost of other things goes up.
"The goal is to provide an investment which has an insurance policy against inflation," a senior administration official said. "We think this is going to be attractive to a lot of people."

This type of bonds has never been offered in the United States but has been used in Canada and Britain. Officials expect individuals as well as pension funds to purchase them as a safe part of a whole portfolio.
The officials said Clinton will also announce plans to broaden the savings bond programme to add some inflation protection to regular savings bonds, which can be purchased for as little as $50.
How the complicated world of U.S. Treasury bond issues has entered the hurlyburly of a U.S. presidential election is a case study in the powers of incumbency.

Knowing that the bonds were under study, Clinton is using them to enliven a campaign trip and stress saving for education, home ownership and retirement -- themes he has repeatedly evoked during this election year.

Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin announced on May 16 that the Treasury planned to issue the inflation-indexed bonds as a multi-year experiment and was studying precisely what form they might take. The securities are designed to strengthen national savings by offering people an investment that guarantees a return that exceeds inflation. The Treasury also expects them to cut its financing costs.
